title: Why a negative times a negative is positive
objectives: Multiply a negative by a positive as repeated losses
Justify why a negative times a negative is positive, from a pattern and from an argument
Use the same sign rules to divide

screens.title: Why a negative times a negative is positive
screens.prose: Losing £3 a day for 4 days is easy to picture. Multiplying two negatives is not, so we will build it from things we can see.
A strategy loses £3 every day. Its running P&L is £0 today.
screens.question: Drag the point to the running P&L 4 days from now.

hints.text: Each day moves the P&L 3 steps left.
Make four jumps of 3 to the left.
After each day: −3, −6, −9, −12.

feedback.correct: Four jumps of 3 to the left land on −12.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Each day is one jump of 3 to the left.

byKey.gain: You moved right, as if each day made £3. A loss moves left.
byKey.added: You took 3 steps and then 4: that adds the numbers. Four days of £3 losses is four jumps of 3.

explain.text: Four jumps of $-3$ land on $-12$. So $4 \times (-3) = -12$. A positive number of losses is a negative total.

screens.prose: Same strategy. It has lost £3 every day for weeks, and its running P&L is £0 today. Now look back in time, not forward.
screens.question: Drag the point to where the P&L stood 2 days ago.

hints.text: Was the P&L higher or lower before the last two losses?
Two days ago it had not yet lost those £6. It was 6 above today.

feedback.correct: Two days ago the P&L was £6 higher: +6.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Go back in time: the last two losses had not happened yet.

byKey.forward: You moved forward 2 days. Two days ago the two losses had not happened yet, so the P&L was higher.

explain.text: Going back 2 days undoes two £3 losses, so the P&L stood at $+6$. Moving back in time through losses takes you up.

canvas.caption: Two days ago the P&L was $+6$

screens.prose: Count days forward as positive and days back as negative. The daily change is a loss, $-3$. Then $$\text{change} = \text{days} \times \text{daily change}$$
screens.question: Which line matches the point you found, 2 days back?

options.why: That is 2 days forward. You looked back, so the days are $-2$.
You kept a minus sign out of habit. But you found the P&L above zero, at +6.
You added the numbers. Each day back undoes a whole £3 loss, so it is a product.

hints.text: How many days, and in which direction?
The point you found sits at +6.
Days back is −2 and the daily change is −3. The P&L you found was +6.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Use −2 for the days back and −3 for the daily loss.

explain.text: The count is $-2$ days, and each day changes the P&L by $-3$. The answer you dragged to was $+6$. So a negative times a negative gives a positive: $(-2) \times (-3) = 6$.

screens.prose: A second view, with no story. Multiply $-3$ by 3, 2, 1, 0 and on down. Each row multiplies by one less than the row above.
screens.question: Fill in the gaps by following the pattern.

hints.text: How much does the answer change from one row to the next?
From −9 to −6 is a step of 3 to the right.
Keep adding 3: −3, then 0, then 3, then 6.

feedback.correct: The answers climb by 3 each row, straight past zero.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Each row is 3 more than the row above.

byKey.r4c1: Below 0 the pattern keeps climbing by 3. After 0 comes 3, not −3.
byKey.r5c1: After 3 the pattern climbs by 3 again, to 6.

explain.text: Each row down adds 3, and the pattern does not stop at zero. So $(-3) \times (-1) = 3$ and $(-3) \times (-2) = 6$. The story and the pattern agree.

screens.prose: Now multiply two negatives straight away. Work out the size first, then the sign.
screens.question: What is $(-4) \times (-5)$?

hints.text: Multiply the sizes first, then decide the sign.
$4 \times 5 = 20$. Two negatives multiplied give a positive.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. The sizes give 20; two negatives multiplied make it positive.

byKey.kept-minus: You have the size right but kept a minus. Two negatives multiplied give a positive.
byKey.added: You added −4 and −5. The question multiplies them.
byKey.added-pos: You added 4 and 5. The question multiplies them.

explain.text: The sizes give $4 \times 5 = 20$. Both numbers are negative, so the product is positive: $(-4) \times (-5) = 20$.

screens.prose: Division undoes multiplication. So $a \div b$ asks: what times $b$ gives $a$? Nothing times 0 gives 5, so we never divide by 0.
screens.question: What is $(-20) \div (-4)$?

hints.text: What number times −4 gives −20?
Count how many jumps of −4 reach −20 from 0.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the number that times −4 gives −20.

byKey.kept-minus: You kept a minus sign. Check: $(-5) \times (-4) = 20$, not $-20$.
byKey.product: You multiplied. Division asks how many times −4 fits into −20.

explain.text: Five jumps of $-4$ reach $-20$, so $5 \times (-4) = -20$ and $(-20) \div (-4) = 5$. Division follows the same sign rules as multiplication, because it undoes it.

screens.prose: You now know that two negatives multiplied make a positive. A common slip grows out of it. Two trades lose £4 and £6.
screens.question: What is $(-4) + (-6)$?

options.why: You used the times rule on an addition. Adding two losses makes a bigger loss.
You multiplied the numbers. The question adds them.
You took 4 from 6 and kept a minus sign. Both are losses, so they pile up to $-10$.

hints.text: Is this a times or a plus?
Start at −4 and move 6 steps to the left.
Adding −6 moves 6 left: from −4 to −10.

feedback.correct: Two losses added make a bigger loss: −10.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. This is an addition, so use moves on the line.

byKey.times-rule: You used the times rule on an addition. Adding two losses makes a bigger loss.

explain.text: Adding $-6$ moves 6 steps left, from $-4$ to $-10$. The two-negatives rule belongs to multiplication only. Two losses added are a bigger loss.

screens.prose: Your results fit four sign rules: $$(+)(+) = +, \qquad (-)(-) = +$$ $$(+)(-) = -, \qquad (-)(+) = -$$ Matching signs give a positive, and different signs give a negative. Division follows the same rules.
screens.question: What is the sign of $(-2) \times (-3) \times (-5)$?

options.why: You saw negatives and used the two-negatives rule once. The first two give $+6$, then $6 \times (-5) = -30$.

hints.text: Multiply two at a time, from the left.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply two at a time and track the sign.

explain.text: Work in pairs: $(-2) \times (-3) = 6$, then $6 \times (-5) = -30$. Each extra negative flips the sign, so an odd number of negatives leaves a negative.

screens.prose: The pattern shows the rule; a short argument proves it. It uses one fact: we multiply a sum part by part. For example, $3 \times (2 + 5) = 3 \times 2 + 3 \times 5 = 21$.
screens.question: Put the lines in order to show $(-3) \times (-2) = 6$.

lines.text: $(-3) \times 2 + (-3) \times (-2) = 0$, multiply the sum part by part

hints.text: Start from a bracket that adds up to zero.
Zero first. Then split the bracket, then use $(-3) \times 2 = -6$, then solve.

feedback.correct: Each line follows from the one before.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Start from the bracket that makes zero.

byKey.m2: That line splits a bracket. Write the bracket first: the line that makes 0.
byKey.m4: That is the conclusion, so it comes last.

explain.text: The product $(-3) \times (-2)$ had to cancel $-6$ to make 0, so it must be $+6$. Any other answer would break the part-by-part rule. That is why a negative times a negative is positive.

screens.prose: A trader is **short** 200 shares: she sold shares she borrowed, so her position is $-200$. Owning shares is the opposite, a **long** position. The price falls from £12.40 to £10.90.
screens.question: Her P&L is position × price change. What is it, in pounds?

hints.text: First find the price change: new price minus old price.
The change is 10.90 − 12.40.
The change is $-1.50$. Then work out $(-200) \times (-1.50)$.

feedback.correct: A gain of £300: she is short and the price fell.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply the position, −200, by the price change.

byKey.sign: You treated the fall as bad for her. Her position is negative, so $(-200) \times (-1.50)$ is positive.
byKey.price-not-change: You multiplied by the new price. P&L uses the change in price, −£1.50.
byKey.change-only: That is the change per share. Multiply it by her position, −200.

explain.text: The change is $10.90 - 12.40 = -1.50$. Then $(-200) \times (-1.50) = 300$, a profit of £300. A short position gains when the price falls: two negatives make a positive.

ideas: A positive count of losses is a loss: $4 \times (-3) = -12$.
Undoing losses moves you up, so $(-2) \times (-3) = 6$. The pattern and the part-by-part argument agree.
Matching signs give a positive and different signs a negative. Division follows the same rules.

formula.name: Sign rules
formula.note: The same rules hold for division, because division undoes multiplication.

summary.trap: The two-negatives rule is for multiplying. Adding two negatives gives a lower number: $(-4) + (-6) = -10$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. The size is 24; decide the sign.

byKey.positive: You dropped the sign. A negative times a positive is negative.
byKey.added: You added −6 and 4. The question multiplies them.

explain.text: $6 \times 4 = 24$, and the signs differ, so $(-6) \times 4 = -24$. Four losses of 6 make a loss of 24.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. The size is 56; decide the sign.

byKey.kept-minus: You kept a minus. Two negatives multiplied give a positive.
byKey.added: You added the numbers. The question multiplies them.

explain.text: $7 \times 8 = 56$, and both numbers are negative, so $(-7) \times (-8) = 56$.

quiz.prose: Division follows the same sign rules as multiplication.
quiz.question: What is $36 \div (-4)$?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the number that times −4 gives 36.

byKey.positive: Check it: $9 \times (-4) = -36$, not 36. Different signs give a negative.
byKey.product: You multiplied. Division asks what times −4 gives 36.

explain.text: $(-9) \times (-4) = 36$, so $36 \div (-4) = -9$. The signs differ, so the answer is negative.

quiz.prose: You hold 300 shares, a position of +300. The price changes by −£0.25.
quiz.question: What is your P&L, in pounds?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply the position by the price change.

byKey.sign: You dropped the sign. You own the shares and the price fell, so you lose.
byKey.added: You added the price change to the position. P&L is position times price change.

explain.text: $300 \times (-0.25) = -75$. A long position loses when the price falls, so the P&L is $-75$ pounds.

quiz.prose: Multiply two at a time, and track the sign.
quiz.question: What is $(-0.5) \times (-0.5) \times (-4)$?

feedback.correct: Three negatives multiplied leave a negative: −1.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply the first two, then the third.

byKey.positive: You made every pair positive. The first two give +0.25, then the third negative flips it.
byKey.quarter: You stopped after the first two. Multiply 0.25 by −4 as well.

explain.text: $(-0.5) \times (-0.5) = 0.25$, then $0.25 \times (-4) = -1$. An odd number of negatives gives a negative.
